text:
Alex: FYI — seeing sustained p99 tail spikes from continuous-batcher since ~03:40 UTC. Affected customer routes intermittently breaching SLO.
Priya: which cluster/pool?
Alex: pool-a (gpu-pool). admission Q oscillating, microbatch sizes jumping 1 -> 8 every few seconds.
Diego: any recent kernel-selector changes or config flips?
Alex: kernel-selector logs show rapid fallback to generic-attn when KV miss rate climbs. each fallback adds ~15-30ms per token.
Zoe: oncall checked nodes — NVLink+mem pressure spikes line up with the tail. no pod restarts but long stalls observed.
Alex: pasted quick scheduler dump (trimmed):
```
[scheduler.dump]
active_batches: 42
avg_microbatch: 1.9 -> 5.8 (10m window)
admission_rps: 340
kernel_path: fused-attn -> generic-attn (flip_count=183)
kv_hit_rate: 0.88 -> 0.56 -> 0.43
cache_evictions: 1200/min spike
```
Priya: that KV churn makes selector flip to the slower kernel, which increases per-request service time -> admission controller reduces batch accumulation window -> smaller microbatches -> higher overhead -> tail.
Diego: sounds like a feedback loop. kernel-selector probably has too-aggressive threshold and no hysteresis.
Alex: I validated on a canary: forcing fused-attn for a minute removed the p99 spikes (~60% reduction).
perf-bot: deploy-bot noticed a canary rollback: 1.14.0 -> 1.13.9 in pool-a at 03:58 UTC (manual rollback).
Zoe: after the rollback p95/p99 stabilized for ~20m. good signal. :thumbsup:  
Priya: proposed mitigation: (1) add hysteresis to kernel-selector, (2) add smoothing for microbatch sizing (inertia on window), (3) limit eviction aggressiveness or throttle noisy tenants.
Diego: I'll draft a kernel-selector PR that introduces hysteresis + flip-rate cap. also add a metric for kernel_flip_rate.
Alex: repro steps + perf capture I used:
```
# metrics
curl -sS http://rtb-1:9090/metrics | grep continuous_batch
# perf capture
perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 10
perf script > out.perf
python3 tools/flamegraph.py out.perf > flame.svg
```
Alex: attaching a small flame excerpt: main tail shows generic-attn hot path and KV lookup stalls clustered at same timeframe.
Zoe: oncall also found a tenant with high write churn around same time — likely noisy neighbor causing KV thrash. I recommend temporary rate-limit on tenant writes + QoS on cache.
Priya: add alert rules: kernel_selector.flip_rate > 5/min and kv_eviction_rate > 200/min per-node. Gate canary for kernel-selector changes.
Diego: will push hotfix PR with defaults: hysteresis=0.15, min_flip_interval=30s, flip_rate_threshold=5/min.
Alex: I'll add the batcher smoothing change (exponential moving average on microbatch target with alpha=0.2) and include config diffs.
Zoe: I'll write the incident timeline and tag affected tenants. creating INC ticket now.
incident-logger: incident INC-2026-042 created and linked.
Priya: owners assigned: Diego (kernel selector PR), Alex (batcher smoothing + perf artifacts), Zoe (incident writeup + tenant mitigation). Target: hotfix PRs within 2h, canary deploy + 30m observation.
Alex: thanks — will upload flame.svg + raw perf logs to the PR. summary coming in #postmortems.
Diego: quick note — consider making kernel-selector consult recent kv_hit_rate weighted by token count rather than raw window (reduces sensitivity to short spike). adding to PR notes.
Zoe: rollback validated stability. leaving monitoring on for 2h.
Priya: follow-up action: add synthetic load test for sustained KV churn to ensure no regression.
Alex: end of thread — ping me if you need the perf artifacts earlier.
